But how long will this favorable cycle last? That's the debate on Wall Street ahead of Micron's fiscal 2026 fourth-quarter results due out Wednesday evening. While a strong quarter is expected, investors might be less focused on earnings-per-share and revenue beats. Instead, they will be more interested in signals about how long the memory shortage will last and whether there will be enough demand as new supply eventually becomes available. Analysts, according to LSEG, expect to see EPS of $31.49 on revenue of $50.9 billion. Micron makes a mix of semiconductor memory and data storage products that have seen demand dramatically outstrip supply thanks to the artificial intelligence boom. The most important products to know are dynamic random-access memory (DRAM) and a specialized version of DRAM known as high bandwidth memory (HBM). Micron also makes NAND flash memory for longer-term data retention. The supply-demand imbalance has led to soaring prices and a windfall for memory and storage stocks. That favorable backdrop has lifted Micron shares nearly 280% this year. Still, the stock remains over 10% below its June 25 record closing price of about $1,213 per share. headlines.article_text: Stocks making the biggest moves midday: AKAM, GENI, PPLI Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Check out the companies making the biggest moves midday: Akamai Technologies — Shares gained 5% after the cloud computing company announced a seven-year contract and $11.6 billion deal with Anthropic on Thursday. Akamai also issued a warrant that gives Anthropic the right to buy up to roughly 5% of the company's shares at an exercise price of $111.33 each. Atlas Energy Solutions — The oilfield and energy logistics stock rallied 17% after the company said that two of its subsidiaries "executed separate cost reimbursement agreements with a leading frontier AI lab." Genius Sports — The sports data and technology stock jumped 13% after JPMorgan initiated coverage with an overweight rating . The bank highlighted Genius' "scarce combo of diversified above-market growth, strong execution, improving profitability/ [free cash flow], and attractive valuation." Twilio — The cloud platform provider with a focus on marketing saw shares tumble about 6%. HSBC slashed its rating to a sell equivalent. "We retain a premium for Twilio's AI optionality, but see negative risk reward post recent rally," wrote analyst Sameer Lam, adding the stock looks expensive compared to "better quality alternatives" like Microsoft and Salesforce. People Inc . — Barry Diller's company, which also owns Food & Wine and Southern Living magazines, saw shares jump 10%. Late Thursday, The Wall Street Journal reported , citing people familiar, that MGM Resorts is weighing a bid to purchase the publishing giant. The news comes after People withdrew its proposal to buy the casino operator. MGM last traded lower by 2%. Scholastic — Shares of the publisher of children's books slid 9% after the company posted a loss in the fiscal first quarter. Scholastic reported an adjusted loss of $3.63 per share, compared with the $2.52 per share loss in the year-ago period. Revenue of $216.8 million reflected a 4% decline from a year earlier. Costco Wholesale — Shares were up 2.7% after the company reported better-than-expected results for the fiscal fourth quarter. Costco earned an adjusted $6.60 per share on revenue of $95.72 billion. Analysts polled by LSEG expected a profit of $6.53 per share on revenue of $94.86 billion. Microsoft — Shares perked up 3% after the software giant rolled out a refreshed Copilot app in a bid to challenge Anthropic's Claude and get more of its enterprise customers to pay for the tools. Meta Platforms — Shares of the Facebook and WhatsApp owner tumbled more than 3% as traders cashed in on the stock's recent rally. The stock is on track for a 12% weekly gain powered by the booming popularity of its consumer artificial intelligence product Muse. — CNBC's Nick Wells and Darla Mercado contributed reporting.
